alt: A hand-drawn map of the valley on aged parchment. Forested ridges ring a central plain: Gaumukh Hill and the Fort Ruins west, Nagadvaja Hill and Mount Dronagiri east, Naga Forest along the north. Between them lie the Village Bazaar and huts, Sheetal Lake, the Mahavidya Temples, Bhoothnath Temple, the Tavern, the Forest Officer's Bungalow and the Professor's Lodge, linked by dashed tracks and the Access Road. A compass rose sits in the lower right.
A wolf stands silhouetted on a cliff edge beneath a full moon, ranges of mountains receding behind it.
A young man at the wheel of a car at night, eyes wide, pressing a folded cloth to his forehead. The windscreen beside him is spidered with cracks.
Seen from high above, a road coils down a forested mountainside in hairpin after hairpin, a single car's headlights drawing a thread of light through the dark.
Close on the driver mopping sweat from his face, one eye screwed shut. An inset panel shows a boulder sitting in the road ahead, lit by the headlamps.
The car strikes the boulder and sparks burst from the impact, the dark valley and a river far below.
A cutaway technical diagram of the car's drivetrain headed Chain Reaction of Failure, with six numbered callouts, repeated underneath as six small panels showing each part giving way in turn.
The car stands skewed across the mountain road at night, front bumper torn loose and hanging, one headlamp still burning. Ridges fall away into the valley behind.
The car comes on down the road towards us, one headlight blazing, its grille punched inward.
A tall night panel. A shaggy figure hangs by one arm from a branch, black against the full moon. Below, at the foot of an enormous tree trunk, the crumpled car lies still.
The moment of impact: the driver is thrown out through the windscreen in a spray of glass, the car folding against the tree.
Extreme close-up of an open eye, unfocused, with peeling plaster filling the rest of the frame.
The ceiling he is staring at: damp-stained plaster between dark beams, a four-blade fan hanging motionless.
He reaches out from the bed towards a glass of water, his right forearm in a plaster cast and his head wrapped in bandage.
He drinks clumsily, water spilling down his chin and bare chest.
He sits up on the edge of the bed. A large room with shuttered windows, an armchair and framed pictures - nothing like a hospital.
Seen from behind, he stands at an open window and stretches both arms wide into the green light outside.
Through an archway, a wide sunlit courtyard with a colonnade running round it and a planted square at its centre.

A study crowded to the ceiling with books, specimen jars and loose papers, a long-necked stringed instrument propped by the window and a bronze figure on a stand. He steps in through the open door, barefoot, his bandaged arm held close.
His own reflection in a window pane: a bearded face under a heavily bandaged head, eyes wide.
The study again, from the doorway. He lies collapsed face down on the floor among scattered papers and a toppled pot.

The lodge in high summer: a low tiled-roof house behind a parched lawn and a row of tall pale trunks, the sun burning white overhead. The Professor kneels in the dust settling a sapling into a bed of flowers.
Close on the Professor turning one leaf of the sapling between his fingers.
He lunges forward with his hand outstretched as a sandalled foot comes down on the sapling. STOMP bursts across the panel.

Over the Professor's shoulder: three men have walked into his compound. A heavy man with a moustache in a dark red lungi, and beside him a tall bare-chested ascetic in white, topknot bound, three lines of ash drawn across his forehead, one hand raised.
Two faces side by side. A stout man in white with a folded shawl, looking uneasy; and the ascetic, his face filling the frame, brows level and eyes fixed.
The ascetic and the Professor close together in profile, the ascetic's hand raised between them.
Villagers stand in a loose half circle under a spreading kadamba tree, where a dishevelled man has both arms flung up.
The ascetic turns his head to the Professor; the Professor looks back at him, mouth open.
The villagers hurl stones. The man under the tree is down on the ground among them.
The moustached man holds a rolled scroll out in both hands; beside him the ascetic stands bare-chested in white, the sun flaring behind the lodge roof.
The ascetic offers the scroll down to the Professor, who leans in with his hand out to take it.
The Professor unrolls the document and reads it at arm's length, the ascetic watching beside him.
The Professor holds the open sheet out, still reading, the ascetic close at his shoulder.
The moustached man pushes the scroll back at the Professor, shouting into his face.
The ascetic lays a hand on the Professor's shoulder and leans in to speak by his ear, his face filling the right of the frame.
Wide shot of the courtyard. The Professor walks away towards the steps of the lodge, his hat slung on his back; the ascetic, the moustached man and the stout man stand together watching him go.
The Professor tips a bowl of water over the bandaged man's head. Splash! Splash!
In the study, the young man sits on the floor propped against a long-necked instrument while the Professor stands over him holding out a glass.
He drinks. In the foreground a pair of hands turns a dark bronze figure with a boar's head and several arms.
The book-lined study. The man sits on the floor at the left; the Professor stands in the middle of the room holding the bronze figure up to the light.
The man pushes himself upright, one hand pressed to his bandaged head, frowning.
The Professor holds up a battered leather book lettered De Rerum Veterum Mysteriis, a crate of loose manuscripts open beside him.
The Professor opens an old palm-leaf manuscript wide in both hands; the man sits below him, hand still at his head.
The Professor stands holding a small worn volume, talking down to the seated man.
Close on the Professor's face, one finger raised, mouth open mid-sentence.
Close on the man's face, eyes wide, sweat on his forehead.
The study again. The man has collapsed face down on the floor, a chair tipping over behind him, papers everywhere, the Professor lunging forward with both hands out.
Seen from behind, the man walks out along the veranda, head bandaged and his right forearm wrapped, into the glare of the dry garden.

The lodge from the road: a long white colonial house with a red tiled roof and a deep pillared veranda, seen through tall wrought-iron gates, its lawn burnt brown and potted plants set out along the drive.
He stands in the garden shading his eyes. Far down the drive, between the gateposts, a figure stands black against the low sun.
He starts back with a shout beside a low circular stone well. A young woman in a long printed kurta sits on the rim with her feet over the edge.
Close: he leans over the well's parapet, his bandaged forearm flat on the stone, looking down the shaft.
The two of them by the well, the lodge behind. He stands with a hand out, talking; she balances barefoot along the rim.
He stands on the burnt lawn with a hand raised, explaining. She walks along the well's rim above him, looking away.
Close on his face, bandage round his head, looking up and answering.
Close on him again, her dark curls falling across the edge of the frame.
Close on her: a mass of dark curly hair, small gold earrings, watching him steadily.
He looks up at her from the grass while she stands barefoot on the rim of the well, the lodge and blue hills behind.
He bends over the well and looks down into the water. Behind him she walks away towards the veranda.
From behind, he walks back towards the pillared veranda of the lodge.

The lodge kitchen. A stout cook in a white cap and a checked towel presses his palms together and bows; the young man stands at the worktop among jars and brass vessels, bright god-prints pinned to the wall behind.
The cook stands with a finger raised, explaining; the young man sits with his back to us, listening.
The two of them with glasses of tea among the brass pots, heads turned to each other.
Close on the cook's face, hand half over his mouth, eyes sliding sideways.
The two seated together, the cook talking with his free hand open, a small cramped balloon behind him.
A high view over the valley: forested ridges folding away on every side with the settlement small in the middle. A little inset map headed The Valley notes that it is ringed by the Himalayan range.
A montage around the cook, who mops his forehead: a steam train trailing smoke, a bus on a hill road, a white car on a mountain bend.
The cook talks with his eyes wide. Behind him hangs a painted forest scene: a tiger, a lion and horned figures half hidden among the trees.
Close on the cook's face, moustache, eyes turned anxiously to one side.
The young man stands in the kitchen doorway looking out at a wall of blue mountains.
A bare stony field under a white midday sun. Dozens of volunteers stoop in rows clearing stones from the ground.
Inside a grand cloth pavilion at the edge of the field, the Mahant reclines against a bolster in white robes, one hand raised in explanation. The moustached man stands behind his couch.
The moustached man tips a whisky bottle; the Mahant sits holding out a glass.
The moustached man drinks while the Mahant talks, one hand open.
A narrow panel: the moustached man draining his glass.
The Mahant turns, hand extended.
Close on the bottle pouring another measure into a glass on the low table.
Outside the pavilion, a working man stands with his brow furrowed, the tents and the sunlit site behind him.

A grid of small frames labelled Night One, Dawn, Night Three, Dawn, Night Five, Dawn. In each night frame he thrashes in bed with a panther and a hooded cobra looming out of the dark above him; in each dawn frame he sits awake, and between them he reads by lamplight.
The lodge lawn. The Professor sits in a cane chair with the young woman beside him; the young man walks towards them across the burnt grass.
The three of them on the veranda, the young woman laughing, the young man's arm in its sling.
The Professor talks with his hand open; Bhavi sits beside him. Behind them the cook comes up the path carrying a brass jug.
The cook pours milk into steel tumblers held out by the Professor and the young man.
The Professor talking, the young man and Bhavi on either side of him listening.
The Professor raises one finger, naming him. Bhavi is on his left, Dvij on his right.
The three of them on the veranda with their tumblers.
Bhavi leans forward pointing, arguing across the Professor.
Dvij, the Professor and Bhavi sitting together, Bhavi looking away.
The Professor holds his tumbler in both hands and answers quietly, Dvij beside him.
Bhavi dabs antiseptic on the gash above Dvij's eyebrow with a swab; the Professor watches from behind.
She presses a plaster down onto his forehead, holding his face steady.
A black inset panel: a struck gong, with the word GONGGGG across it.
The Professor turns with a hand out; Bhavi stands stiffly with her arms down; Dvij sits between them.
The Professor talking; Dvij seated; Bhavi turning away, her hair swinging out.
Bhavi stands with her arms folded, the Professor seated in the middle, Dvij at the right.
The Professor with a hand at his chin, thinking; Bhavi and Dvij both turned towards him.
A large close-up of Dvij's face, the plaster on his brow, looking levelly out of the frame.
Dvij walks out through the open door into the bright garden. The Professor sits at his desk with his hand at his mouth; Bhavi watches him go.

Inside the Mahant's tent. The Mahant reclines against bolsters in white, one hand raised; Dvij stands with his back to us, the moustached man beside him. A low table holds a bottle, glasses and a spread newspaper.
Close on the Mahant, topknot bound, three stripes of ash across his forehead, smiling narrowly. Dvij's shoulder fills the foreground.
Dvij kneels with his palms joined; the Mahant sits facing him among the cushions.
Close on the Mahant with his fingertips pressed together, grinning.
Dvij kneels on the carpet while the Mahant lays a hand flat on his head. The moustached man and the stout man stand watching; a Sanskrit verse hangs on the tent wall behind.
Dvij stretches full length face down at the Mahant's feet. The two men watch.
A large close-up of Dvij's face, plaster on his brow, speaking.
The Mahant's face and raised hand fill the panel, eyes wide, mouth open, proclaiming.

Outside in the open. A square fire altar burns before a young sapling, heaped with fruit and flowers. The Mahant strides forward with one arm out, Dvij and the two men following; rows of villagers in white sit cross-legged on the ground. A Sanskrit verse is printed on the tent behind.
The Mahant, seated, beckons Dvij to sit beside him where the crowd can see.
Dvij sits at the Mahant's side among the seated villagers, palms together.
Close on Dvij, eyes closed, palms pressed together. A mantra in Devanagari fills the balloon beside him.
Hands tip ghee from a long ladle into the fire; baskets of fruit stand at the altar's edge.
Close on the Mahant's face, smiling, rudraksha beads at his throat.
The moustached man stands to one side, arms loose, watching.
The Mahant rests his hand on Dvij's bowed head beside a lit lamp.
Close on Dvij's face, plaster on his brow, eyes turned away.
A wide landscape at day's end: Dvij walks alone across bare ground towards a wall of mountains, the tent, the fire and the crowd small behind him at the left.
Dvij walks a dirt track past a muddy pond where villagers are working waist-deep. Thatched huts, a dog, a column of smoke, a timber building up on the rise.
Dvij on a plank bridge as a train of laden mules crosses it. CREAK!
A man lies fast asleep on his stomach along a shop counter, price boards and a hand-lettered notice on the wall behind. ZZZ.
A tavern at a crossroads of two dusty paths: a tumbledown shack, half brick and half bamboo and thatch, men sitting on benches outside.
Inside the tavern. Dvij comes through the doorway; the milkman in a red turban sits talking with two friends under the price boards.
Dvij flings an arm out to block a man hurrying away.
Dvij stands over a seated man, pointing down at him and asking.
Dvij leans in close, finger levelled at the moustached man, who sits back.
The man throws an arm out, pointing away across the room.
Under a thatched shelter, a gaunt man eats at a rough table while Dvij walks up from the right, bag over his shoulder.
The gaunt man leans over his plate, eyes up and wary, flies circling him; palms and huts in the heat behind.
A hand held out open, offering. Dvij stands at the right under the thatch.
Dvij in profile, listening.
The gaunt man, eyes wide and flies around his head, with Dvij facing him across the table.
The gaunt man throws both palms up in refusal, shaking his head. Dvij leans in over a plate of food and a steel tumbler.
The gaunt man's hands tremble in front of him; Dvij leans right across the table, close to his face.

A yard at sunset. A battered blue van stands among the scrub, roof rack piled with bundles, one door hanging open. Viraat stands beside it; Dvij watches from the right with his hands in his pockets. An inset at the top left shows Dvij's face.
Inside the van: Dvij perched on a wooden stool, gripping the frame of a shattered window, mountains showing through the broken glass.
Viraat hunched over the steering wheel behind a spidered windscreen.
A narrow strip: a misted gorge dropping away beside the road.
A steep stony track climbing between cliffs into cloud.
Inside the shaking van, Dvij and Viraat both wide-eyed. RATTLE! KNOCK!
Viraat at the wheel, mouth open in fear. Behind him the dark forest is full of shapes: huge shaggy man-figures, crouching ghouls, a horse-headed being.
Close on Dvij, unimpressed. Beside him, as if remembered, the Mahant in white with a scorpion crawling across his robe.
The van labours up a rutted forest track, sound effects bursting all round it: BRRRAAA, RRRATTLE, CLANG, THUD, KLANG, CHUNK.
Close on Viraat, sweat running, teeth bared, both fists on the wheel. RRRATTLE!
A brown boot stamping down on a worn pedal, loose bolts and bare wiring under the dash. KLANG!
The view out through the cracked windscreen: a mountain road pitted with craters, a small framed deity and a tassel hanging from the dash.
A wide view of the forest road switchbacking up the mountainside as the light goes, the van tiny on a bend far below.
At twilight the van passes the wrecked blue car lying at the roadside, Viraat looking across at it.
Dvij turned in his seat, and his own face again in the cracked wing mirror, the wreck receding behind.
A cutaway of the engine tearing itself apart in smoke and sparks. SPLUTTER! WHEEZE! SNAP!
The van stands dead on the forest track, a wisp of smoke rising. Silence.
The van begins to roll backwards down the slope, both men still inside.
Dvij leaps out of the moving van against a burning sunset sky while Viraat scrabbles at the ground beside the wheels.
The two of them heave a boulder in behind a rear wheel.
The van stopped at last, seen side on, a figure sprawled on the ground beside it.
Viraat lies flat on his back on the stones, spent.
A narrow view past the cliff edge to dark ranges under the last of the light.
Dvij stands at the drop, hands at his sides, looking out over the valley.
Dvij sits on a roadside milestone with his chin on his fist. Viraat waits by the van; a thread of smoke still rises from it.
Dvij walks away down the road; Viraat throws out a hand after him.
Dusk on the mountain road. Viraat hurries after Dvij, the van small behind them.
The wrecked blue car lies nose-in against a huge tree trunk under a night sky, its front crushed and its headlights gone. The two men stand looking at it.
Dvij crouches at the driver's door with a light. Two insets: an intact seat belt buckle, and keys still hanging in the ignition.
Viraat grabs Dvij by the shoulders and hauls him back from the car.
Both men flinch as something gives way in a burst of splinters. CRACK!
Dvij sits in the wrecked car turning the key; Viraat leans in at the passenger door. Two small insets: a hand holding the key ring, and a bundle of cut wires.
The two of them sitting in the car talking, the dashboard dials between them.
A big close shot of both faces: Dvij open-mouthed, Viraat's eyes wide, the shattered windscreen webbed with cracks behind them.
Dvij's face ringed by four smoky vignettes: a pair of hands, a walking silhouette, a woman's face, a blood-stained bundle.
Two small panels: the broken bumper being wrenched free, SCRAPE!, and Dvij passing half of it to Viraat.
Dvij at the wheel of the rolling car with Viraat beside him, mountains coming up through the cracked windscreen.
The car pitches down the slope in a shower of sparks, CRASH and BOUNCE across the panel; beside it, a man lies spread-eagled on the grass.
Dawn on a grassy slope. The car lies wrecked and smoking; Dvij and Viraat lie flat on their backs beside it.
The study. The Professor stands with a hand to his chest; Dvij sits at the left with his forearm grazed and bloodied; Bhavi is curled in a chair at the right in a green dress.
The Professor puts a hand to his head over the desk; Bhavi leans forward from her chair, arguing; Dvij sits below.
Dvij leans forward answering; the Professor stands between them; Bhavi sits hugging her knees.
The Professor raises a hand to explain; Dvij gestures back; Bhavi watches from her chair.
The Professor standing between the two of them, Dvij looking up at him, Bhavi turned away.
Dvij talks with a hand out; the Professor bends down towards him; Bhavi rests her chin on her hand.
Dvij talking, with an inset above him: the Mahant reclining in his tent between the moustached man and the stout man. Bhavi listens from the right.
The Professor hauls a large old volume down from a high shelf; Dvij and Bhavi watch from below.

The Professor lays an old chart on the table - a Vaastu Purusha Mandala, a squared grid with a sprawled figure drawn across it and the directions marked round the edge. Dvij leans in at the left, Bhavi at the right.
The Professor throws an arm up as he tells it. Behind him, painted across the wall, gods in a starry void hold down a giant man lying face first. Dvij and Bhavi listen from the right.
The Professor points up at a diagram of a cosmic temple, circles inside circles with planets around them. Dvij and Bhavi look up at it.
The Professor talks with both hands open beside the Vaastu Purusha Mandala chart propped on the table; Dvij stands with his arms folded, the temple vision spread behind them.
The Professor at the window, the mandala chart lying on the table in front of him.
Dvij turns with a hand out, Bhavi beside him.
The Professor seated with the chart, answering.
Dvij and Bhavi sitting together, she looking at him.

A wide view of the study. A large hand-drawn map of the valley is spread across the table; Dvij leans over it on both fists, his grazed forearm showing. Bhavi throws her hands up at the left; the Professor stands at the right with one finger raised, mid-shout. On the floor is a book titled Architecture of the Vastu Shastra, and a jar of rudraksha beads on the shelf.
A corner of the room by the window, with a caption about the crude razor and its stinging lather of herbs and salt.
A weathered board reading Ravenswood Park at the head of a stone-edged trail; a figure with a backpack comes up it.
Dvij's face, shaved for the first time - a few days' stubble gone, the plaster still on his brow and a healing cut on his cheek.

Bhavi in a printed sundress in deep forest, shafts of sun coming down through the canopy, turning a small flower in her fingers beside a stream. A carved sign points to the Scenic Trail, Overlook Point and Picnic Grounds.
A narrow strip of the forest path between mossy stones.
Bhavi walking on through the tall grass and sunlit trunks, a satchel on her shoulder.
Dvij stands with his hand at his chin. Bhavi is at a wooden signpost wound about with strings of cloth, beads and flowers.
The signpost close up, its arms reading Overlook Point 1.8 miles and Picnic Grounds 0.7 miles under the offerings tied round the post. Bhavi walks away down the path.
Dvij and Bhavi facing each other on the trail, he talking with a hand open.
The two of them walking on together under the trees.
Remembered frames stacked like photographs: children running in a garden, a family group, a man at the park gate. Bhavi stands in front of them.
More remembered frames - a crowd of faces, a woman gathering a small girl in - and Bhavi telling it, with Dvij listening beside her.
Bhavi and Dvij side by side on the forest path, she turning to look at him.
The two of them on the sunlit trail, Dvij answering with one hand raised.
Close on both faces, Dvij with a hand flat against his chest.
Seen past Dvij's backpack, Bhavi climbs a flight of old stone steps up into the trees.
The two walking on, Dvij talking with a hand out.
They stop face to face on the path.
Bhavi stands with her arms folded, a signpost behind her.
Dvij explaining, Bhavi beside him with her jaw set.
Dvij gestures with both hands open.
Bhavi rounds on him, one finger out.
The two walking apart, Dvij pointing back at himself in disbelief.
Bhavi turns away; Dvij stands behind her by another signpost.
Bhavi jabs a finger at him; Dvij spreads his hands.
Dvij's face fills the panel, alarmed, shouting a warning over the forest path.
Dvij stares while Bhavi throws her head back laughing. Behind her stands a tribesman in a tall feathered headdress and fur, holding a long staff.
The Soma village: a clearing ringed by low thatched huts and tall trees, cooking fires smoking, people working and children running. Dvij and Bhavi walk in with the tribesman.

A craftsman in a feathered crown works at a forge, sifting metal in a bowl. Four insets show a dhokra peacock figure, hands pressing wax threads, molten metal being poured, and a bowl of finished gold-coloured pieces. Dvij and Bhavi watch from the right.
The village again, people moving in from all sides towards something; Dvij and Bhavi among them.
A shaman bursts out into the open, arms up, in a spray of white motion lines.
The shaman contorting in the middle of the clearing while the drums go Beat... beat... beat. Dvij and Bhavi watch from behind.
Dvij in profile; Bhavi beside him explaining, the shaman a blur of movement behind them.
The shaman whirling, hoops of motion drawn round him, beside a big earthen vessel. Bhavi watches from the left. Beat... Beat... Beat...
A tribesman tips a jar and pours a golden liquid into the vessel, ranks of villagers standing behind.
The shaman lifts the jar over his head and drinks, the liquid running down.
Dvij and Bhavi in the crowd, she with a finger at her lips hushing him. Behind them the shaman drinks from a raised jar beside the drums.
The shaman spinning in the open, BEATBEATBEATBEAT across the top of the panel, drummers and villagers round him.
The shaman with both arms flung wide among the villagers, until he stops. Dvij and Bhavi watch from the left.
Dvij and Bhavi close together, watching the dancer whirl past.
Bhavi startled, the dancer close in front of her, his head swinging loose.
Dvij and Bhavi standing before ranks of villagers, a long drawn HAANAA rising on both sides.
Dvij with a hand up, objecting; Bhavi answering, a big earthen casket behind them.
Three narrow panels: a man slumped on the ground, a man stooping at the casket, a man reeling backwards.
The crowd pours in around the casket, cups held out, liquid slopping over the rim.
Dvij grinning; Bhavi turning to him, alarmed.
Dvij walks off through the crowd with a cup already in his hand; Bhavi puts out a hand to stop him.
A bedroom. Dvij rubs his eye while Bhavi pushes the shutters open on a burning sky.
Dvij sits up on the bed talking, pleased with himself; Bhavi stands at the window with her back to him.
Dvij still knuckling his eye; Bhavi laughing at the window, the sun low behind her.
Three remembered frames: the tribesman and Bhavi holding Dvij up between them, the three of them lurching, and all of them going down in a heap.
Close on Dvij, the grin gone.
Bhavi folds a cloth, not looking at him.
Dvij on the edge of the bed with both palms raised.
Bhavi walks out through the door into the orange light, a bundle under her arm.
Dvij stands alone in the bedroom. On the wall behind him a warm glow holds the shape of Bhavi's face.
The Professor at his desk under a wall of charts and a carved mask, manuscripts spread everywhere, pen raised, looking up sharply as Dvij comes in.
The Professor leans across his desk with two fingers raised, delighted; Dvij listens at the right.
The Professor talking with both hands; Bhavi behind him with a palm turned up in protest; Dvij at the edge of the frame.
The Professor points up at a framed picture of the feathered shaman on the wall; Dvij watches.
The Professor in full flow, fingers spread; Bhavi with her head in her hand; Dvij thinking. On the wall behind, charts and a numbered list naming Patanjali, Panini and Katyayana.
The Professor with both arms up, shouting happily; Bhavi covers her face.
A printed plate headed The Great Panini, with a portrait of the sage and a table of his rules. Dvij looks up at it; the Professor holds up a finger at his desk.
The Professor at his lamp-lit desk, one hand raised, laying out his challenge.
Bhavi throws both hands up, asking where.
Bhavi and Dvij at the desk, pressing him.
The Professor raises a finger and answers; Bhavi turns sharply.
A vast fortress wall of cut stone with a square tower and a tall arched gate. Dvij and Bhavi are small figures at the foot of it.
The ramparts from inside, arched galleries running along the top of the wall.
Dvij and Bhavi climb the path where it bends between the walls, she pointing up at the stonework.
The two of them close against the wall, Bhavi with a hand raised towards it.
Dvij, startled, one hand going to his collar.
Bhavi, level and unimpressed.

A wide view of the open plateau beyond the gates: a small carved stone temple standing among scattered ruins, an orange flag on a pole, langurs sitting in a spreading tree. Dvij and Bhavi in the foreground.
Dvij and Bhavi among a stand of leafy plants.
The two turned away from each other.
Bhavi points down at the shatavari leaves.
Bhavi raises two fingers, explaining the name.
A large close-up of Dvij, eyes wide.
Dvij turns away with a hand at his neck and a small embarrassed smile.
Dvij climbs a steep flight of stone steps up the outside of a round tower, pack on his back; Bhavi is already well above him.
From the top of the tower the whole valley opens out: boulder-strewn slopes, a lake catching the light, rain falling far off. Dvij and Bhavi stand at the parapet looking over it.
The two close together, Dvij talking, Bhavi watching him.
Dvij with a hand behind his head; Bhavi smiling to herself.

A vision behind them: giants heaving boulders over the fort walls, and a horned rakshasa riding a mountain through the sky while Indra looses the vajra at it. Bhavi explains with her hand up; Dvij listens.
More of the vision - giants flinging rocks, and a meteor breaking into burning fragments over the valley. Bhavi and Dvij stand below it.
A large close-up of Bhavi, half smiling; Dvij in the panel below, looking out.
Dvij with a hand at his chest; Bhavi glancing back at him.
Dvij and Bhavi standing close at the parapet, he looking away, she watching him, the sunlit valley behind.
The sky has gone black with rain. Dvij puts a hand up to his head; Bhavi turns her face to the downpour with her arms opening, delighted.
The two of them running along the top of the ramparts in the rain.
They scramble down a grassy slope towards an isolated pillared temple among the rocks.
Under the temple's stone portico they look out at the rain sheeting over the valley.
Inside the ruin, Bhavi stands with her arms crossed while Dvij holds a phone up towards a window, hunting for a signal.
Dvij at a broken archway, face turned up; the clouds are breaking and blue is coming back.
Bhavi stands in the ruin looking down at the phone in her hands.
A hand holding the phone: the photo app, image 312 of 487, showing a girl with long curly hair turned to the camera against a stone wall.
Bhavi in the foreground holding the phone; behind her Dvij runs his hand over a carved stone doorframe.
Dvij points at a shape cut into the wall - a hanging loop like a noose - with Bhavi close at his shoulder.
Three narrow panels: Dvij photographing the carving, Dvij standing back to frame it, Dvij holding the phone up with the flash firing.
Dvij has gone over backwards in a puddle, legs up, phone still held high, stars spinning round his head. Bhavi crouches beside him, entirely unsympathetic.

A great stepped tank: tier upon tier of stone steps descending on every side to green water, with a small stepped shrine standing in the middle and temple towers around the rim. Dvij points it out; Bhavi looks over the edge beside him.
The two of them bent almost double, crawling into a low stone underpass where a channel runs down into the tank.
Dvij and Bhavi on hands and knees at the mouth of the underpass, looking out along a shallow channel of clear running water.
They come out into the open beside the stream, ruins and rocks rising behind them.
Bhavi has rolled up her salvar and stepped into the water, turning back to wave Dvij in.
The two of them walking upstream side by side, shoes in hand, water round their ankles.
The Mahavidya temples: ten carved spires of white, yellow and red crowded behind a low wall, the gate shut, a board in Hindi giving the hours. Dvij and Bhavi stand looking in.
Under a mango tree, village children reach up for fruit. Bhavi walks past with a red dupatta over her shoulder; Dvij is behind her, taking a photograph.
The village edge: mud-and-thatch huts along a rutted track, children sitting in the dirt, and a painted sign reading Achhut Basti. Dvij and Bhavi walk in.
An old woman crawls on all fours in front of a broken hut, her hands and feet bandaged. Dvij stares; Bhavi answers him without moving.

Bhavi tells it with a finger raised, Dvij listening. Behind them, in ragged-edged memory frames: a preacher haranguing a village crowd, a woman tending a patient on a cot, people turning away, a hut in darkness.
Dvij kneels in the dust and tips water from a bottle into the cupped, bandaged hands of the old woman. Bhavi stoops over her from the other side.
Dvij close to the old woman's face; her hand has closed on his wrist.
A close shot of the two hands, her gnarled bandaged fingers under his palm.
Bhavi rounds on Dvij, hand on her hip; the old woman kneels between them with her palms together. Small framed faces of staring villagers run down the left edge.
Villagers crowd in on all sides as Dvij and Bhavi walk through; a wiry man breaks from the ranks to follow close behind.
A strip of small panels: the crowd closing in, faces pressing forward, the old woman among them.
Dvij and Bhavi push through the packed street, villagers on every side.
Bhavi hurries ahead down a lane while the wiry man skips after her; more villagers follow.

A strip of small panels of the two of them running through narrow alleys, then a wider view as they break into dense green at the forest edge. Dvij and Bhavi stop among the trees, talking; the patter of following feet has stopped behind them.
The Mahant asleep on a bed of white bolsters, one eye cracking open in irritation.
He sits up on the bed. Through the arched window a burst of comic-book noise rises from the street below.
He walks out barefoot onto a carved wooden jharokha balcony overlooking the crowded bazaar.
Indoors, the moustached man sits in a chair with a hookah pipe; the Mahant stands over him with a hand out, a painted goddess on the wall between them.
The moustached man draws on the pipe while the Mahant raises a finger.
A dancing woman appears in the doorway, sees the moustached man and stops; the Mahant flicks his fingers and she is gone.
The Mahant turns towards the door, barking at whoever is knocking; the moustached man smokes on.
Close: Kurup's scarred face at the left, the Mahant's at the right with a finger at his lips.
Kurup crouches low on the tiled floor, holding up an ornate metal figure.
Kurup, hunched and grinning, presents the figure while the moustached man leans in behind.
The Mahant lounges back dismissing him; Kurup backs away across the hall.
A grand colonial bungalow standing derelict under a burning orange sky, its walls swallowed in creeper, windows black, the gateposts leaning. Dvij and Bhavi are small at the gate below.
The two of them in front of the house, Bhavi with a finger up, warning him off.
Dvij hauls himself over the top of a stone wall while Bhavi reaches up after him, her dupatta flying.
The two of them pushing through the overgrown shrubbery along the wall.
A hand forces a broken window frame open. RANKLE! The sound echoes into the dark inside.
Dvij climbs in through the window and reaches back to take Bhavi's hand.

Inside: a great ruined entrance hall, a chandelier hanging in shafts of dusty light, a double staircase, hunting trophies of a tiger and a stag mounted on the walls. Dvij and Bhavi stand small at the foot of the stairs with a torch.
The two of them moving down a corridor hung with old portraits, the torch beam thrown ahead of them.
Dvij lifts a rifle out of a rack of guns, torch beam along the barrel; Bhavi leans in beside him.
An office with a mounted stag's head and a brass nameplate for the Forest Officer, R. N. Pratap. Dvij holds up a bundle of files; Bhavi has a wooden crate open in front of her.
The two bend over an open ledger of visitor numbers and a printed revenue chart; Dvij runs his finger down a column. A park map lies beside it.
Two moments side by side: Dvij at the desk turning a small bronze figure over in his hands; then he presses its arm, CLICK, and a bookcase swings out from the wall. Bhavi watches.
A narrow stone stairway dropping away into blackness; the two of them stand at the top with the torch.
Dvij shoves a tall mirrored dressing table across the library floor.
Moonlight comes through the window past an oil lamp and strikes the tilted mirror.
The mirror throws a shaft of silver light down into the dark; Dvij and Bhavi stand in the beam.
Close on Dvij in the stone passage, hand at his chin, puzzling it out.
The two of them hurrying along a vaulted tunnel of dressed stone, torch held out ahead.
In the tunnel, Dvij puts a hand on Bhavi's shoulder; she covers her face. A small light lies on the stone between them.
A skeleton lying on the tunnel floor, skull turned towards them, one side of it broken away.
A blank stretch of tunnel wall.
The two of them crouched over the skull, Bhavi's finger at the hole in its side.
Bhavi turns away and puts a hand flat against the wall.
Dvij hauls at a chained iron grille at the head of a stone stair, moonlight coming through the bars.
The two of them at the grille, Dvij reaching up, Bhavi behind him.
Close on Dvij's face at the bars, looking out.
Close on Bhavi at the bars, a hand on the ironwork; through the gap a moonlit temple spire.
Dvij raises one finger.
Bhavi turning, then answering; Dvij with his finger still up, the chains and the night beyond the gate.
Dvij yawns hugely, Bhavi beside him in the dark tunnel.
Dvij looks up; Bhavi rests her chin on her hand and smiles at him.
The study. Dvij points across at Bhavi, who has come in wearing tall riding boots; the Professor sits at a board game he has been playing against himself.
The Professor turns with a hand out, approving; Bhavi stands with her hands on her hips; Dvij watches from the left.

The Professor holds up a finger and explains, Dvij and Bhavi leaning over the desk. Down the left and along the bottom run small framed images: a matted-haired ascetic, a skull bowl, sadhus at a fire, a temple, a trident and ritual beads.
Dvij and Bhavi walk out along the garden path towards the gate, arguing cheerfully.

The Kaal Bhairava temple: a small many-tiered stone shrine standing on a spit in a still lake, a densely forested hill rising behind it, huts along the far shore, vultures turning overhead and smoke from the cremation ground.
The temple steps, flanked by carved vyalas - elephant-headed lion creatures on high plinths - with panels of gods and beasts cut into the soft stone above. Dvij stands at the bottom looking up.
Inside the temple: carved pillars rising into shadow, a lingam lit at the far end. Dvij and Bhavi come in from the left past seated sadhus.
The inner hall, ascetics sitting before the shrine with skull bowls beside them.
Bhavi waits in an ante-room among the pillars while sadhus sit at a fire beyond; flames climb the right edge of the panel.
Dvij and Bhavi bow beside a fire. Facing them sits the tantric baba, cross-legged, matted hair down his back, bands of ash across his chest and brow.
A big close shot of the baba, beard and dreadlocks, firelight on his face, speaking.
Dvij in profile at the left, the baba across the fire, Bhavi at the right.
Dvij bows with his palms together; the baba raises a finger; Bhavi watches.
Dvij, head lowered, answering; the baba listens; Bhavi looks on.
The baba rises and begins to walk in a circle round the two of them as he teaches.
Dvij kneels with a hand at his chest; Bhavi covers her mouth; the baba stands over the fire.
Dvij asks across the fire; the baba answers with a hand at his chest, a small shrine figure lit behind him.
A wide band: Dvij and Bhavi at the left, the baba in the middle with a finger raised, and a younger ascetic with a topknot and strings of beads at the right.
The baba goes on speaking while the young ascetic, at the right, opens his mouth wide.
A circular inset of Dvij's and Bhavi's shocked faces beside a close view of the ascetic's open mouth, an arrow curling back into his throat.
Dvij and Bhavi recoil, Bhavi's hand at her mouth, as the tongue disappears back down the throat.
The same moment from another angle, the baba impassive between them.
The baba raises a finger and explains; the young ascetic beside him; Dvij and Bhavi seated at the fire.
Dvij and Bhavi sit close together; the baba leans in towards them across the flames.
The baba raises a finger, telling Dvij whose attention he has caught. Bhavi sits between them with her hand at her chin.
A woman stands in the firelight: long curling hair, a leopard-print top, heavy tribal jewellery at her throat and arms, looking straight out of the panel.
Close on Dvij, turning to look.
Bhavi turns to the baba with a hand raised, alarmed, while the woman leans in behind him and whispers at his ear.
Dvij scrambles back with both palms up; the baba rises over him, pointing.
The baba stands with a finger raised over the fire, Dvij backing away at the left and Bhavi at the right.
At the left, a memory: the woman bending over Dvij where he lies, blood at his shoulder. At the right the baba raises his finger again while Dvij answers him and Bhavi looks away.
Bhavi and Dvij walking a dirt track, Bhavi arguing over her shoulder. Some way behind them, among the trees, the woman in the leopard-print top is following.
The two walking on, Dvij protesting with a hand out. In the corner, a purple-edged memory: the woman bent over Dvij where he lay bleeding.
Bhavi stops and jabs a finger at Dvij, who stands with his arms folded.
The lodge seen from its wrought-iron gates, the drive running up between dry lawns. Dvij walks towards the veranda with Bhavi behind him.
Two narrow panels: Bhavi pushing the front door shut, then turning to look back out through it.
Bhavi drops onto a sofa with her arm flung along the cushions and her eyes shut.
Bhavi at the window. Beyond the curtain, out at the gate, the woman is standing quite still.
The Professor with a hand at his chin, asking.
Dvij with a finger raised, answering.
The Professor and Bhavi sitting among shelves of stone sculptures, Bhavi turned away from him.
The Professor close up at his board game, a fist on the table, questioning. Rows of small stone Buddhas on the shelf behind.
Dvij stands telling it with a hand out. Beside him, in cloudy remembered frames: the two of them entering the pillared temple, ascetics round a fire, the baba's hall.
The Professor leans forward with both hands raised; Dvij sits listening, the game board between them.
Dvij, still standing, asks a question.

The Professor answers with a hand out; Bhavi listens at the right. Behind them, in smoky frames: Naga tribesmen with spears, uniformed settlers with rifles, women hiding their faces, a burning village, and a wounded tiger.
The Professor talking, a hand raised.
Dvij, arm behind his head, half listening.
A shout in jagged red letters: THE SKELETONS!
Dvij lurches forward open-mouthed; Bhavi recoils beside him.
The Professor throws both palms up, appalled.
A run of small panels: the Professor turning, Dvij explaining, Dvij pointing and grinning, Bhavi dismayed, and the Professor and Dvij face to face again over the board.
Dvij at the left and the Professor at the right; between them a thought-cloud shows a saffron-robed messenger standing in a temple courtyard.
Bhavi raises a finger, teasing; the Professor turns on her, indignant.
A large close-up of Dvij, appalled.

Dvij with both hands to his head. Beside him, bright vignettes: a golden figure reclining on a serpent couch on a milk-ocean, a calendar disc of the lunar months, and a temple by a river with crowds. The Professor and Bhavi stand at the right.
Dvij with his palms together, pleading; and again in close-up, wretched.
The Professor raises a finger and announces he is coming too; Bhavi at the right.
The Professor talking, Dvij and Bhavi on either side of him.
The Professor with a hand out, challenging them; Dvij looks back at him.
Bhavi presses her palms together and asks, the Professor half turned away at the left.
The Professor leans in, warning; Dvij and Bhavi listen.
The Professor with a hand at his chin, Dvij beside him.
Bhavi with her hands together, asking for one more.
A big close-up of the Professor's face, light glinting off both lenses of his spectacles.

The dining hall by the light of a single oil lamp. Dvij and Bhavi sit at the table with steel dishes in front of them; the cook stands behind in a white turban and checked towel, carrying a pan. Lamplight throws long shadows over the walls.
Dvij and Bhavi lean towards each other over the lamp, the flame between their faces.
Dvij raises a finger. Behind him, in a remembered frame, the little temple and the cremation ground.
Bhavi sits back with her mouth open, seeing it.
Dvij and Bhavi facing each other, both talking at once. Two small frames above: a skeleton in a tunnel, a temple, and a not-equals sign between them.
Dvij with a finger up and Bhavi leaning in; and again beside it, Dvij making the same point.
A diagram over the table: a crescent moon, a tilted mirror on its stand throwing a beam, and the mouth of the tunnel. Dvij and Bhavi work it out across the lamp.
A small night map: the moon at west, an arrow curving north-west to a temple spire.
Dvij and Bhavi both open-mouthed as the name lands.
The Professor, white-haired in the lamplight, sits on a sofa with a finger at his lips, listening.
Bhavi alone at the table, the flame in front of her, unhappy.
Dvij and Bhavi across the lamp, he telling her what he means to do.
Bhavi with her arms folded, looking away.
Dvij props his chin on his hand, smiling; Bhavi leans right into his face, furious.
Dvij looks up. On the wall behind him, Bhavi's shadow has grown a pair of horns; she is already walking out of the room.
A hand comes down and pinches out the flame of the brass lamp.
A narrow strip of the darkened room.
The Professor's face close in the dark, a hand at his mouth. On the wall behind him, a horned shadow.
A sliver of the room's edge.
The Professor turns sharply in his chair, one hand going to his chest.
He pulls the shutters closed across a window.
He presses the slats flat, then hurries across the room past the shelves of stone figures to his desk.
The Professor bent over the desk, pen in hand, drawing on a sheet of parchment.
The finished parchment: line drawings crowded over it - a crescent moon, three circular emblems, a row of small standing figures, a scatter of leaf shapes, a spoked disc, a bull and a horned animal.
The Professor lies down along the sofa in his overcoat without putting out the lamp, eyes open.
He folds the parchment and slips it inside his coat by the light of the oil lamp.

A huge crowd fills the temple ground from edge to edge - thousands of people between market stalls with Hindi signboards, striped pavilions, the lake and a great temple beyond, forested ridges closing the valley in.
In the bazaar, traders weigh out grain and spices at a stall hung with bangles, a decorated goat is led through the press, and villagers crowd the lake's edge.
The Professor at the left; Dvij and Bhavi beside him in the crowd, Dvij looking off towards the noise.
Two of the Mahant's men in red turbans take Dvij by the arms and steer him away; he waves back over his shoulder, grinning.
Bhavi throws an arm out after him, dismayed; the Professor stands at her shoulder.
Inside a great cloth pandaal, rows of seated men under the canopy.
Dvij is led through the packed pandaal by men in turbans.
A procession on the dais: the moustached man, Dvij, and shaven-headed priests in garlands of marigold, with the stout man behind them.

On the garlanded dais the Mahant stands with one arm thrown up, addressing the gathering. Dvij, the moustached man, the Professor, the stout man and other dignitaries sit behind him in marigold garlands; a sea of turbans fills the foreground.
From behind Dvij's shoulder, the crowd runs unbroken to the horizon under a hazy orange sky, temple spires on the skyline.
The Mahant jabs a finger sideways at Dvij, who sits beside him looking bewildered; the moustached man and the Professor are on either side.
The moustached man mops his face with a cloth in the blazing sun; Dvij sits fanning himself; the Mahant goes on talking.
A folk theatre begins on the platform: a performer in a turban and skirt dances while others watch from the wings.
Two dancers in full costume, one in blue and gold, one in red, caught mid-step.
Musicians in orange turbans playing a tambourine-like kartal and a long-necked taanpura.
The row of dignitaries on the dais - the moustached man, Dvij, priests, the stout man - with the crowd below. In a circular inset, Bhavi's face looking up out of the turbaned throng.
A large close-up of Dvij in his garland, eyes tired. Beside him, half-remembered, the dark yogini's face, and the Professor at the right.
A young man in a gold-bordered dhoti sits cross-legged with a finger raised, golden question marks and flourishes spiralling out of him; villagers press in from every side.
The Professor, delighted, explains to Dvij with both hands; other listeners behind them.
The expert seated in the middle of a ring of ten numbered points, each one a questioner, the whole gathering around him.
A chart held up beside a pointing finger: 1. Forward sequence, the numbers one to ten with arrows; 2. Backward sequence, ten to one; 3. Skipping syllables, with alternate numbers dropped.
The Professor talking on with his hand up; Dvij beside him; the moustached man at the right.
SHHHHH! Several of the dignitaries turn and hush the Professor; Dvij hides a smile behind his hand.

Deep night on the ceremony ground: a priest sits before a garlanded lingam surrounded by brass vessels, lamps and offerings, the crowd thinned to a few. Down the left edge a list of the offerings - milk, ghee, curds, honey, rosewater, sesame oil, sandalwood paste.
Dvij yawns hugely behind his hand, eyes streaming; the Professor beside him is wide awake.
The Mahant lifts a conch to his lips and blows. BWOOOOM! Dvij watches from the foreground.
The Mahant makes the offering before a seated stone deity. Two framed insets: water poured over the deity's feet, and water offered in a spouted vessel. Dvij watches at the right.

The priest dresses and garlands the deity. Framed insets around him show water streaming over the image, the garlanded figure, and incense smoking in a dish. A line of labels runs along the bottom: milk, ghee, curds, honey, rosewater, sesame oil, sandalwood paste.
The priest raises the lit aarti lamp before the dressed and garlanded deity, smoke curling up on both sides.
The fire altar at full blaze. Priests feed ghee into it with long spoons while Dvij, beside them, sags with his eyes shut, sweat on his face.
The Mahant blows the conch again - BWOOOOM! - and Dvij jerks awake, open-mouthed, while the priests sit with palms joined.
Dvij asleep on his hand beside the fire; the Professor leans past him, arms out, entirely awake.
The Professor crouches to whisper with a priest, arrows showing him darting from one to another, while Dvij dozes on.

A printed plate headed with the Professor's explanation: eight numbered steps - the land purified, a pit dug, a golden kalasha filled with earth, the ground laid out as a Vaastu Purusha Mandala, nine gems, nine grains, nine minerals, and the foundation stone placed - each with its own small illustration.
The Professor talks on with an arm flung wide, beaming; Dvij has given up and is asleep on his fist beside him, the fire still burning behind.
The Professor's face and Dvij's side by side against a field of stars and violet light, Dvij's eyes half closed.
The Professor hauls Dvij upright by the arm and walks him away from the lamplit ground; in a small inset, Dvij doubles over as feeling comes back into his legs in yellow jags.

A village lane at night: an old musician sits cross-legged under a thatched lean-to bowing a long stringed instrument, listeners in the shadows, a lantern beside him. The Professor walks Dvij past, taking his weight.
The Professor puts a hand out to fend off a wall, Dvij slumped against his shoulder, a lamp burning on the gatepost behind.
Indoors, Dvij reaches for a bed by lamplight and stops.
The bed is already taken: Bhavi lies there in a lilac nightdress, propped up on an elbow, half awake.
Dvij crouches by the bedside talking to her, the lamp between them.
The Professor comes in briskly through the door with a coffee pot in one hand and a mug in the other, the dawn garden behind him.
A sliver of Bhavi turning her head on the pillow.
Dvij sits on the edge of the bed with a hand out, suggesting they move; Bhavi lies back with her arms folded.
Dvij sluices his face from a basin of water; beside him, Bhavi dries hers on a towel.
The three of them in the study: Dvij at the left, the Professor in the middle with a coffee cup, Bhavi at the right against a wall of books, a globe and a brass armillary sphere.
The same three, the Professor drinking, steam rising from the cup; Bhavi listening with her head turned.
The Professor leans towards Dvij and levels a finger at him.
The Professor in profile; Bhavi beside him with a tear on her cheek.
A close-up of the Professor's face, grave, one finger raised.
Bhavi's face, eyes wet, looking up at him.
The Professor turns away, a hand at his coffee, not looking at her.
Bhavi, tears on her face, a hand at her chest, promising.
The Professor sits back with his fingers laced together, satisfied.
Dvij leans in and objects.
The Professor raises a finger, delighted with himself.
Bhavi throws a hand up in protest; the Professor sits between them with his chin on his hands; Dvij grins at the right.
All three round the desk over a spread of charts, Bhavi with her hand out asking where to begin.
Bhavi laughs; the Professor raises a finger; Dvij thumps a fist into his palm.
The Professor turns to the two of them and sets his condition, both of them watching him.
A large close-up of the Professor, one finger up, about to speak.
The three heads together over the desk, the Professor giving them the clue.
Through the study door, the Professor walks out into the green garden with his hands clasped behind his back. Dvij and Bhavi watch him go from the table.
Bhavi, now in a green kurta, turns to Dvij with both hands open, asking. He lounges back on a bench under the shelves of stone Buddhas, snow peaks through the window.
Dvij shrugs with a hand out; Bhavi props her chin on her fist, unimpressed.
Close on Dvij, working it through aloud.
Close on Bhavi, asking who.
Close on Dvij again, answering.
Close on Bhavi, her eyes narrowing.
Dvij leans forward with both hands open, stung.
Bhavi folds her arms and looks away.
Bhavi stands and turns her back; Dvij stays on the bench looking up at her.
Bhavi at the window with her back to him; Dvij asking from the bench.
Bhavi, arms crossed, sets her condition; Dvij sits looking up at her.
Bhavi walks out barefoot; Dvij half rises with a finger raised, calling after her.
A man bursts in and goes sprawling - gaunt, scarred down one cheek, in a mud-coloured kurta - scattering a bronze figure across the floor. Dvij lunges after him; Bhavi stands at the door.
Dvij gets an arm round the man's neck and wrestles him down among the toppled things.
STOP! in jagged red letters. Bhavi shouts with a hand out; the two men are locked together, hands at each other's throats.
A wide panel: the fight broken up, the Professor making introductions with a hand out, and then Dvij and the scarred man shaking hands while Bhavi stands between them with her arms folded.
A close-up of Dvij, grazed, explaining himself.
A close-up of the scarred man - Kurup - pitted skin and wary eyes, giving his account.
Dvij, unconvinced, asking a question.
Kurup talks with both hands, Bhavi listening; then the Professor and Dvij together at the right.
The Professor, both hands up, demanding to see it; Bhavi and Dvij at the edges of the frame.
The Professor grabs Kurup by the shoulder, delighted, while Bhavi and Dvij watch.
All four of them on the floor sifting through the scattered rubble and broken pieces, the mountains bright through the window.
Kurup holds up a bronze figure of a celestial nymph in a triple-bend pose, hands raised in a gesture of wonder. The Professor leans in with his eyes wide; Bhavi and Dvij crowd behind him.
A large close-up of the statue's face - heavy crown, lowered eyes, earrings and necklaces - with a hand reaching towards it.
The Professor recoils, appalled.
The Professor cradles the statue, looking at the damaged ear.
Kurup jabs a finger at Dvij, protesting; the Professor stands between them.
Dvij spreads his hands and apologises.
The Professor with a hand at his chin, thinking it over.
Dvij and Bhavi turn to Kurup, who answers, pointing up the mountain.

Dvij and Bhavi walk a deserted village street under a burning red dusk, doors bolted and shutters closed on either side. A tall temple spire rises black against the sky. A Hindi notice is painted on a wall.
The same street at dawn, waking up: people moving between the houses, the temple gate ahead.

The temple seen through its gateway: a great tiered stone spire above a wide wet courtyard, with a milkman carrying churns across the foreground. A technical drawing of the temple plan runs down the right edge.

Inside the compound. A carved stone lion on a plinth, more spires behind. A pot-bellied attendant with ash stripes across his chest turns to face them; Dvij and Bhavi are seen from behind as he leads them down a narrow alley.
A grid of small panels of the Mahant's morning: waking on his bed, ritual bathing, sitting in meditation, a private meal of many dishes, a public meal, and receiving petitioners.

A pillared marble hall with high lattice ventilators, its ceiling painted with a chariot and horses from the epics, dancer figures carved on the pillars. Dvij stands gazing up; Bhavi speaks to him sharply from the right.
The Mahant enters and settles on a central bench, one leg crossed over the other, attendants ranged behind him. Dvij stands at the left, Bhavi at the right.
Dvij talks with both hands open; the Mahant sits impassive, an attendant beside him; Bhavi watches from the corner.
Three close panels in a row: the Mahant with a finger raised, Dvij asking, the Mahant's face hardening.
The Mahant levels a finger; Dvij answers him; the Mahant again, jaw set.
Dvij at the left, the Mahant's face in the middle, Dvij again at the right, the questions coming one after another.
A narrow strip at the foot of the hall.
Dvij stands among the seated villagers with his palms together; the Mahant glares from the right.

Dvij gestures at a scene behind him: a village schoolroom, a blackboard with a book, a sun diagram and a map of India, children on benches and a teacher. The Mahant listens, furious; men in caps and turbans behind him.
Rows of villagers looking on, the Mahant among them with his arms folded.

In the temple compound a mahout on an elephant's neck sponges down its hide. Dvij and Bhavi walk past, talking; saffron-clad priests move away behind them, and the great gate tower rises over everything.
Dvij in profile with the Mahant behind him and one of the moustached men beyond, warning Bhavi off.
The courtyard filling with people in dhotis and shawls.
Bhavi and Dvij face to face, close, arguing in low voices.
Bhavi with a hand at her chin, turning the question back on him.
DONG! DONG! The temple bells swing; priests and Bhavi stop where they stand.
Dvij climbs the steps to look; the Mahant stands a couple of steps above and behind him.
CLAMOR! in big letters over the gate tower as people run in towards the entrance from every direction.
A mendicant in rags capers in the street, arms flung out, villagers backing away.
The crowd turns on him; a man draws his arm back to throw.
The mendicant staggers as stones come in from all sides.
A narrow strip of the watching crowd.
Dvij remembers the tantric baba: the ascetic seated by his fire, one hand raised, with three painted figures of renunciation on the wall behind - a robed ascetic, a trident, and a matted-haired god.
Dvij turns and speaks up, the temple crowd behind him.
The Mahant swings round, furious, beads at his chest, the temple wall behind him.
Dvij and the Mahant nose to nose, both in profile, neither giving way.
The Mahant flings an arm out down the steps, ordering him; priests stand behind; the mendicant crouches at the bottom.

Bhavi, alarmed, names the plant; Dvij, pointing down at the papers, asks if she remembers what her uncle said.
A narrow strip of the room.

A remembered scene: the Professor at a table in a tribal settlement, an illustrated book open in front of him, talking with Dvij while the whole process runs along the bottom - stems washed, crushed in a mortar, pressed, filtered through a skin, mixed with milk pouring into a bowl of stars. A large close-up of the Professor at the right, one hand raised, refusing to say more.
Dvij talks with both hands open under the desk lamp, Bhavi listening. Beside them, a page of Rig Veda verses in Devanagari and a glowing golden figure standing in a bowl of light.
Bhavi answers over the open leaf album; beside her, a plate of red-capped mushrooms and a painting of tall tawny stalks growing at the edge of a lake.
Dvij points; beside him a chart from the Sushruta Samhita showing twenty-four kinds of soma plant in a grid, with mountains along the top.
Dvij, hand at his chin; Bhavi levels a finger at him.
Dvij raises a finger; Bhavi and Kurup listen. Below, two insets: the Professor among bearded tribal elders, and a pile of old manuscripts.
Dvij, Bhavi and Kurup round the desk. Two small frames: the Professor reading, and a lamplit room of shelves.
Bhavi with a hand at her chin; beside them, a golden emperor enthroned with nine advisers ranged behind him.
Bhavi talks; Dvij and Kurup on either side; a laptop screen glowing with a search box in a starfield.
A narrow strip of the desk.
Dvij talks on; below, small charts of Vedic chronology, a modern scientific timeline, the ascent to Pitruloka, and transmigration.

Larger plates: thirty-three devas becoming thirty-three koti devas; the golden cosmic egg beside a figure shaping a world; and Vedic chronology - the yugas turning on a wheel, a mahayuga of 4.32 million years against one day of Brahma - set against the Western age of the universe at 13.8 billion years.
Dvij, hand open, says he does not think her uncle meant them to look for the plant.
Bhavi, hand at her chest, asks why not; Kurup listens at the edge of the frame.
Dvij and Bhavi over the open album, she arguing back.
Dvij with a hand out, Bhavi with her chin on her hand, Kurup at the right. An inset: the Mahant bent over a chest of gold and jewels.
Dvij and Bhavi close together, both intent, the pressed leaves between them.
Dvij talks with a hand open; beside him a golden bowl of glowing liquid; Bhavi at the right, unimpressed.
Bhavi raises a finger, conceding the point.
Dvij and Bhavi over the desk while Kurup doubles up coughing at the right. An inset: carved figures standing among boulders on a hillside.
Bhavi points; Kurup answers. Three insets: a spiral conch, a dark fossil ammonite, and the Mahant with his treasures.
Dvij spreads his hands and asks how any of it relates to a leaf; Bhavi looks back at him across the album.
Bhavi, hand open, suggests not taking the leaf literally. Beside her, a small panel: a leaf with an arrow turning it into a glowing seed-shaped emblem.
Dvij, finger at his chin, asks where that leaves them; Bhavi and Kurup on either side over the leaf album.
Dvij grins and points, pleased with his own joke; Bhavi folds her arms.
Dvij spreads both hands; Bhavi holds up a flat palm and tells him nobody is laughing.
The three of them bent over the parchment on the desk again, Dvij smoothing it flat.

The study settles into work: Dvij sprawled upside down over the arm of a chair with a sheet held above his face, Bhavi curled in the sofa reading, Kurup cross-legged on the floor. Small sound words drift about - whistle, sigh, cough.
The same room from the other side, the lamp on the desk, all three reading in silence under the ceiling fan.

Dvij upside down on the chair with a sheet; beside him a drawn plan showing eight small buildings arranged in two overlapping squares, an arrow turning them into the elevation of the lodge's back wall. Bhavi glares from her chair; Kurup looks up from the floor.
Bhavi's face, furious.
Dvij, upside down and smug, says he cracked it long ago; Bhavi looks ready to throttle him.

The convalescence room next morning: the Professor propped in bed in bandages, Dvij sitting forward on a stool beside him, Bhavi in an armchair, Kurup standing at the wall, and the cook cross-legged at the foot of the bed.
Dvij close, a hand at his chest, admitting he has an approach rather than a solution.
Bhavi, chin lifted, tells him to go on.
Dvij raises a finger: every clue needs a key, and who made this parchment?
Kurup answers at once - the master - the Professor asleep behind him.
Dvij, working it forward.
Bhavi asks how they are supposed to do that.
Dvij explains his plan: three vantage points, one each.
Kurup speaks about what he saw in the Professor, a fist closed.
Dvij listening.
Bhavi at the left; Kurup telling how his own people turned on him after the tiger.
Bhavi, quiet, listening.
Dvij asks what about his work.
A large close-up of Kurup, talking about the objects he brought from the forests and hills.
Bhavi answers, about the books and about being loved more than them.
Dvij and Bhavi sitting together by the bed, Bhavi with a hand raised: everything was symbolic of some hidden truth.
Dvij paces the room with a hand at his chin, Bhavi watching from her chair.
A narrow strip of the room.
Bhavi asks what he is thinking; Dvij turns with one finger up, the answer arriving.
Dvij's feet crossing the rug; then Dvij with a finger raised, naming it - iconography, the study of symbols.
Bhavi, chin on her hand, and Kurup beside her, taking it in.
Dvij holds up a sheet headed Iconography, with an om sign, a lotus, a dancing many-armed figure in a ring of symbols, and a trident drawn on it.
Bhavi, hand at her cheek, watching him.

A hand holds the parchment up: its drawings now read as three ruled rows, each numbered - the tree, crescent and discs in the first; Ganesha, the line of small figures and the leaves in the second; the pot, the spoked disc and the bull in the third.
Dvij leans over the parchment and points along a row; Bhavi looks on.
A strip of the parchment with the crescent and discs lined up.
Bhavi and Dvij close together, both seeing it: each row is a puzzle, five rows means five solutions.
Kurup asks whether each row has to be solved on its own, the Professor asleep behind him; Bhavi holds the parchment up at the first symbol, the tree.
Dvij with one finger raised, explaining that it is the only image in the first row.
Kurup, hand at his chin, saying it makes no sense to him.
Dvij, smiling, says he has solved it.
Bhavi, unimpressed, asks what the secret message is.
Dvij gives the name.
Bhavi's face, mouth open, astonished.
Dvij explains beside the Professor's bed, Bhavi at the right: whatever they are looking for will be in the Gyaneshwar temple.
Kurup turns with an objection; Bhavi and Dvij look round at him.
Kurup, raising the problem; Bhavi's hand comes into frame.
Dvij at the bedside, the cook and the sleeping Professor behind, Kurup pressing the point: there is no Gyaneshwar temple in the valley.
Dvij sits forward with his hands clasped; Bhavi and Kurup at the right, and an inset panel of a crowded temple complex labelled 108.

Kurup asks how he got from a tree with an eye to Gyaneshwar. Below, two plates: the drawn tree with a vertical eye in its trunk; and that eye with an arrow to a meditating Shiva, the third eye on his brow, crescent in his hair.
Bhavi, hand at her chin, beside a plate of the same tree-with-an-eye.
Kurup shouts the name with a finger up; Dvij and Bhavi behind him. Below, a small equation of symbols: tree plus trident plus crescent plus lingam equals tree.
Bhavi, hand open, turns to Dvij; Dvij answers over her shoulder.
Dvij raises a finger beside the sleeping Professor; below, a plate of blue-throated Shiva in meditation with a trident.
Dvij makes a joke about wringing someone's neck; Bhavi holds up a flat palm at him.
A narrow strip of the room.
Dvij and Bhavi close together; Kurup jabs a finger from the right, insisting there is still no such temple.
Bhavi raises a finger: the vertical eye can only mean Shiva. Beside her, the plate of the eye and trident again.
Bhavi points; beside her a plate of a fierce blue deity with a garland of skulls. Dvij at the right, sweating.
Dvij and Bhavi in the sickroom, Bhavi with a hand out; beside them, a dark many-tiered temple lit by two braziers with a guardian face over the door; Kurup at the right.
Outside the lodge gates: Dvij and Bhavi walk away down the track while the yogini in her leopard-print wrap comes through the trees behind them.
The yogini spins with her arms out, motion lines whirling round her, shouting.
Bhavi, hand at her chin, wondering aloud; Dvij, at the right, answers.

A wide vista: the Kaal Bhairava temple on its stone causeway out in a lake of still water, lotus pads at the edge, the low sun blazing off the surface, forested ridges all round and smoke rising from the far shore. Dvij and Bhavi stand small at the water's edge, seen from behind.

Inside the temple: a gilded gateway to the inner shrine where a vertical eye-shaped lingam stands garlanded in the dark. Dvij and Bhavi walk in past hanging lamps; a priest half dozes beside the offering bowl.
Dvij and Bhavi close together, looking at it, Dvij naming the eye they came for.
Bhavi, hand at her cheek, asks about the tree.
A priest with three lines of ash across his brow and a string of beads, one finger at his lips.
Dvij, cheerful, says to look around.
Bhavi, hand at her chin, beside a carved stair rail and lion: the friezes are full of trees, but not the one.
Kurup scratches his head in the temple hall; Dvij and Bhavi turn to him. Beside them, a grove of tall straight-trunked trees in the ashram compound.
Dvij, hand at his chin, stands beside a carved temple guardian - a lion-faced beast rearing on a pillar.
The same beast in close-up: horns, bared fangs, bulging eyes, a heavy mane of carved curls.
Dvij talks with a finger raised. Beside him, a remembered frame of the Professor at a board game, and a caption comparing a temple's vertical structure to a tree.
Dvij points at a diagram: a temple tower and a tree drawn side by side to the same height, the underground kalasha matching the roots and the plinth matching where the trunk leaves the ground.
The tree half of the diagram, doves perched in its crown.
Dvij gestures at the full diagram again, the temple's proportions measured against the tree's.
A large drawing: the temple tower standing inside the silhouette of a great tree, its roots spreading below and its canopy above - the whole temple as a tree.
Bhavi, hand at her chin; Kurup leans in behind her. Beside them, two plates: the drawn tree with the eye in its trunk, and a black lingam with the same eye and three bands of ash.
Kurup, finger raised, saying the hole is visible only from the sanctum; Dvij answers; Bhavi and Kurup look up at the ceiling.

A measured elevation drawing: the sanctum, the pillared hall, a tall lamp column and the gateway tower, with a dashed sight line running through them and a caption asking whether the hole aligns with the dhwajastambha and beyond.
Inside the temple, Dvij points up at a hole in the ceiling; a beam of light runs from it down to the lingam. Bhavi and Kurup watch.
Outside: a tall brass-clad lamp column with a flag at its top, the beam of light striking it, the gateway tower beyond.
Bhavi, working it out, asks if the eye is looking at the lamp column.
Dvij answers - or at whatever is beyond it.
A close view up the column to the flag and the sky.
Kurup, alarmed, asks what is beyond it.
Dvij says they can only know from the front porch.

From inside the porch: the monolithic Nandi bull on its plinth, the lamp column, the golden gateway tower - and behind everything, an enormous mountain filling the sky at sunset. Dvij, Bhavi and Kurup stand looking out at it.
Bhavi, now in a teal kurta, holds up the second row of the parchment - a crescent and four small discs - while Kurup flings an arm up; Dvij sits behind with his chin on his hand.
Bhavi holds the row out and says they must read all the symbols together; Kurup offers that the discs are three chakras of Vishnu.
Bhavi asks about the moon, holding the strip up.
Kurup, delighted, says the moon is Shiva's, and together they make Harihara; Dvij watches from behind.
A plate of the two gods becoming one: four-armed blue Vishnu at the left, a trident-bearing Shiva at the right, and between them the composite Harihara on a lotus, labelled.
Dvij raises a finger, spinning it in a circle, and asks to borrow the scooter.
Bhavi's faded pink scooter propped against a sack marked Panchkavya in a dusty shed.
Dvij crouches at the scooter in the yard; Bhavi and Kurup watch with folded arms and ask how he will drive it with no petrol.
Dvij grins - you'll see.
Dvij running.
Dvij works at the scooter while Bhavi and Kurup stand by.

Dvij crouches at a car with a jerrycan and a length of hose, siphoning fuel; then he tips the scooter over to drain the tank, and finally pours petrol in from the can while Bhavi claps her hands together and Kurup looks on.
Dvij drives the pink scooter along a dirt track with Bhavi riding pillion, her dupatta streaming out behind; hills on one side, reed beds and water on the other.
A crowd of shepherd boys swarms the scooter, laughing and grabbing at Dvij's shirt as it ploughs through a herd of cattle and goats in a cloud of dust.
Bhavi has been shaken off and runs after them through the sheep, arms out, shouting.
The boys still hanging off Dvij and the handlebars, hauling at his sleeve.

A star chart: the zodiac's twelve signs in a ring of roundels - Mesha, Vrishabha, Mithuna, Karka, Simha, Kanya, Tula, Vrischika, Dhanus, Makara, Kumbha, Meena - drawn round the sprawled figure of Kaal Purusha in the constellations, with a crescent moon at the edge.
Dvij and Bhavi sitting in the grass under a huge tree, the scooter propped behind them and the herd moving off in the distance; then the two of them riding home along a lake at sunset.
Dvij, Bhavi and Kurup at the desk over an open book and a nakshatra table. Above, three emblems labelled Bharani with Venus, Ardra with Rahu, Dhanishta with Mars.
Bhavi repeats the word back, startled; Dvij, hand behind his head, starts to explain; Bhavi holds up a flat palm to stop him.
Kurup stabs a finger at a card showing the three nakshatras with their initials - B, A, D - and shouts that it spells bad. Bhavi and Dvij look at him.
The card again with the letters spelt out under it - B, A, D, BAD - Kurup delighted, Bhavi appalled, Dvij with his chin on his hand.
A large close-up of Kurup talking about how pundits use the nakshatras to name a child. Above him, a plate reading Sacral name: GOTILAL.
Kurup holding up two fingers; Dvij collapses over the table laughing; Bhavi hides her face.
Bhavi sits bolt upright with a finger raised - it's a name.
An oil lamp on the desk; and Kurup, straight-faced, saying Gotilal is his given name.

A chart headed Nakshatra Syllable Chart: three columns of syllables under the three nakshatras, one circled in each, combining to make a name. Below it, Bhavi with a finger up, telling Kurup it is the coded message that spells a name.
The three of them bent over a worksheet: three columns of syllables, a note to pick one from each column, a list of eliminated combinations, and Dvij explaining. An oil lamp burns at the right.
A rejected combination struck through: Lekugi?
Another struck through: Pothagi?
A third struck through, Pochhage?, with Kurup below it, hands at his chin, thinking.
PONGA! bursts across the panel as Dvij slams a finger down on the worksheet, where the three chosen syllables - Po, ng, ga - flow into the name.
All three round the sheet, Bhavi wide-eyed, Kurup frowning: Ponga, the dotty mendicant.
Night: a ragged figure crouched under a great tree with hanging roots at the forest edge, and the party crossing the dark village below the fort wall with the yogini alongside.
Kurup squats down beside the tree, then straightens and walks briskly away as Dvij comes up behind him.
Dvij crouches with a hand held out to Ponga - a wild-haired old man in rags, matted beard, down on all fours.
Kurup holds out a plate of rotis; Ponga reaches for it with both hands, eyes huge.
Dvij looks off to one side, working something out.
Dvij stands alone looking up at the great dark mountain under a full moon, the fort lights small below.
The procession walks back towards the lit windows of the lodge: Dvij, Kurup with a roti held up, Ponga shuffling after it, and the yogini alongside.

Dinner round the low table by the light of a coal stove, the power gone: Kurup, Dvij and Bhavi eating from steel dishes, the cook at the stove behind, and Ponga hunched on the floor with an onion and his rotis.
Dvij, alarmed, hears the plan said out loud.
Bhavi, hand on the table, says her uncle is still unconscious and may be in a coma.
A dark corridor of the lodge with a lamp at the far end; Bhavi in the foreground saying they must go before the Mahant does.

Dvij's mock-formal roll call under the bare bulb, five captioned portraits in a row: Forest scavenger, half his face lost - Kurup; Suspicious stranger, memory lost - Dvij himself, arm raised; Gibberish-spouting beggar, sanity lost - Ponga; Mystic maiden, language lost - the yogini in the doorway; Doctor, patience intact - Bhavi with her arms folded.
Kurup holds up a small cooking pot like a trophy; behind him, a hand-drawn map of the mountain with the summit at 24,700 feet, a glacier and a base camp marked.
Dvij holds up a rolled sleeping bag under the bare bulb.
Bhavi holds up a white first-aid box with a red cross, the mountain map behind her, a hurricane lamp lit on the table.
Dvij holds up a striped blanket and a small packet, teasing her.
Bhavi raises a finger, worried about the Mahant; Dvij and Kurup at the table; Ponga eating in the corner.
Kurup jerks and sends a dish of yellow dal flying in an arc; Dvij and Bhavi recoil.
Kurup crouches to gather up the spilt food, explaining it away as a draught.
Dvij, Bhavi and Kurup look up at the shuttered windows and closed doors - there is no draught.
A large close-up of Dvij, smiling to himself over a bundle of papers.
Bhavi rounds on him, pointing, in front of the mountain map with its base camp and ravine marked; Dvij looks back at her.

Night outside the lodge: Bhavi stands in the lit doorway, Kurup walks off towards the shed, and Dvij steps out onto the gravel path as the last light goes out. The mountain stands black against the sky.
Dvij, still smiling, spreads a hand; Bhavi turns away. A file marked Case Notes, Patient: Prof Iyer, lies on the desk.
The lodge gates under a full moon. Dvij walks down the drive; the yogini crouches by the gatepost in the dark.
A close-up of the yogini's face, tense, her tribal necklaces catching the moonlight.
A close-up of Dvij, looking back at her.
Dvij comes to the gate and puts out his hand; the yogini crouches at his feet.
She takes his hand and rises; the two stand facing each other in the moonlit garden, a dog watching from the shadows.
